children: Shares of SG Mart Ltd. fell another 6% on Thursday, November 26, following a 20% fall on Wednesday, and an 18% cool-off from the day's high during Monday's trading session, when the stock had ended with losses of over 5%.

The stock fell after the company cancelled its Board of Directors meeting scheduled for Thursday, citing the non-availability of directors. In an exchange filing dated November 25, 2026, under Regulation 29 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the company said the meeting—which had been intimated on November 22, 2026, was called off without announcing a revised date.

SG Mart's board meeting had been slated to consider a proposal to raise funds through the issuance of equity shares, convertible securities, or other permitted instruments. Potential fundraising routes mentioned in the earlier notice included a preferential issue, rights issue, qualified institutional placement (QIP), or a combination of methods, subject to applicable laws and approvals.
With this fall, the stock is down around 40% from the highs on Monday.
Market watchers also pointed to broader group-related sentiment after Tata Steel announced plans to acquire a controlling stake in APL Apollo Tubes.

Because both SG Mart and APL Apollo Tubes share common promoters in the Sanjay Gupta-led group, sharp selling in APL Apollo Tubes and peer group names added to nervousness around SG Mart, even though SG Mart has not formally linked the drop to that transaction.
Shares of the other Sanjay Gupta entity SG Finserve are also trading with losses of 6% in today's session.
Shares of SG Mart are now trading 6.8% lower on Thursday at ₹770. Ahead of the fall, the stock was up over 125% so far on a year-to-date basis.

title: SG Mart shares down 40% from Monday's high after cancelling board meet for fund raise
